sentences.text: [Name of our group, who we represent, and how many families we are in touch with.]

sections.heading: Why we are writing to you

sentences.text: We are writing because DYRK1A-related intellectual developmental disorder and UBE3A-related Angelman syndrome are recorded on the same mechanism road: too little protein from loss of one copy, with definitive gene-disease links in both conditions.
The phenotype similarity score between the two conditions is marked high.
Angelman syndrome also has more established infrastructure, including patient organizations, registries, and targeted clinical trials.
Both conditions have definitive gene links in Gene2Phenotype.
Both curated mechanisms are recorded as loss of function, inferred from variant types.
Shared informative features include inappropriate laughter, happy demeanor, abnormal demeanor, social disinhibition, and abnormal response to social norms.
Registry design and natural history protocol are marked transferable.
Outcome measures and endpoints are also marked transferable, but age of onset and severity still need review before any instrument is adopted.
Clinical network, sites, and investigators are marked transferable as well.

sections.heading: What we would like to learn from or reuse

sentences.text: We would like to learn from your registry design, natural history protocol, and consent materials.
We would like to learn which outcome measures and endpoints your community has found practical to collect.
We would like to understand how your community built its clinical network and connected families to sites and investigators.
We would also like to review trial design templates, such as population, endpoints, and duration, because these are marked as a credible template pending expert review.
For Angelman syndrome, targeted trials were found, but no disease-specific approved therapy was found.
We must not assume the two communities share the same exact mechanism in every family.
For UBE3A, published cases document variants acting in more than one direction, and published claims disagree with the curated mechanism.
Mechanism is recorded per gene and disease, not per family, so a child's own variant must be confirmed by a clinical geneticist before acting on transfer ideas.
The curated mechanisms for DYRK1A and UBE3A are inferred from variant types rather than functional studies.
A UBE3A animal or cell model cannot stand in for a DYRK1A model.
The assay design may still be reusable on the same road, but only with expert review.
The listed Angelman organizations and registry listings passed automated checks of their own sites, but the listings are marked unverified.
Enrollment in an Angelman trial is not asserted for a DYRK1A family.
Which direction for UBE3A do you consider established, and on what evidence?
Is the listed Angelman patient organization the right contact, and does it run a registry?
Has our child's specific DYRK1A variant been functionally classified as loss of function, gain of function, or dominant negative, and does it match the mechanism recorded for the condition?
What functional evidence exists for DYRK1A?
Can Angelman trial design elements be adapted for DYRK1A without assuming the same treatment strategy will apply?

glossary.meaning: A change that lowers how well a gene works, often leading to too little working protein.
The biological way a gene change is thought to cause the condition.
A study that follows people over time to learn how a condition changes.
An outcome a study measures to judge change over time.
A doctor who interprets genetic test results and what they may mean for a person.
A lab cell or animal system used to study a condition.
